identityReview: Julia Eileen Gillard, Australian politician born 29 September 1961 in Barry, Wales, migrated with her family in 1966. Melbourne LLB 1986 and BA 1989 are recorded separately. First woman prime minister, 24 June 2010–27 June 2013; party loss on 26 June is a different event. Earlier deputy-premier and ministry end dates differ. GPE chair 2014–2021 and Beyond Blue chair 2017–2023 are former roles, with continuing Beyond Blue patronage. Wellcome Board chair from 12 April 2021 is corroborated as current in October 2026; GIWL founding chair and Hakluyt international advisory membership remain distinct from executive or government posts.
lifeStatusEvidence: University of Melbourne’s 20 October 2026 report describes Gillard’s actual Climate CATCH Lab oration and preceding roundtable, with direct attributed remarks, as current Wellcome chair. The exact event date was not independently established. Hakluyt’s 19 October appointment announcement adds contemporary role evidence. A 9 November FT indexed interview excerpt is newer corroboration, but its full body was behind a subscription wall and is not represented as read.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read National Archives fast facts and selected before-office, during-office and timeline sections; NFSA metadata and selected speech transcript; GPE appointment release; Brookings dated biography paragraphs; King’s institute announcement; Wellcome appointment/current-role pages and annual-report chair-date table; Gillard’s December 2023 statement and Beyond Blue succession release; Hakluyt company announcement on AAP; Melbourne’s October 2026 event report. Read Commons and original Flickr descriptive/licence text without image pixels.
corrections: Read the National Archives fast-facts profile. It gives 29 September 1961, Barry, Wales; University of Melbourne LLB 1986 and BA 1989; Lalor membership 3 October 1998–5 August 2013; deputy premiership 3 December 2007–24 June 2010; and education, employment/workplace relations and social-inclusion portfolios ending 28 June 2010. The premiership ended 27 June 2013. Do not merge degree years, ministerial end dates or parliamentary retirement with the premiership. The chief-of-staff role was with Victorian opposition leader John Brumby, not the then premier.

Read relevant early-life and student-politics sections of the Archives narrative. It records the family leaving Southampton on 7 February 1966 and settling in Adelaide, study in Adelaide and transfer to Melbourne, student-organising roles and transition into legal work. The departure date is not independently established as the arrival date. Its broad combined Arts-Law description is less precise than the fast-facts degree years. Its closing prose overstates the length of her deputy premiership as three-and-a-half years; use the explicit 2007–2010 dates instead. No original migration file or degree certificate was inspected.

Read the Archives account of the 24 June 2010 swearing-in, negotiations after the hung parliament, 14 September new ministry, and the 26–27 June 2013 transition. Four crossbenchers supported government formation; Bob Katter supported the Coalition, so not all named independents joined Labor’s support arrangement. The Greens’ formal agreement ended in February 2013. The party ballot on 26 June and effective resignation/new Rudd swearing-in on 27 June are distinct. Party selection of a leader is not a nationwide direct election of prime minister.

Read selected Archives timeline entries on 2010 leadership/election, carbon pricing, 2013 education funding, disability support and resignation. It distinguishes carbon-pricing announcement, legislation and planned commencement, and records education legislation passing the Senate on 27 June 2013 and NDIS establishment in March before the July launch. The public highlight describes the government’s reform agenda, not an independently audited long-term outcome or sole personal achievement. Do not claim all rollout occurred while Gillard remained prime minister, or that every original policy remains in force today.

Read NFSA’s collection description and selected transcript passages, confirming the 9 October 2012 parliamentary speech responding to Tony Abbott in debate concerning the Speaker. This was political argument, not new legislation. The later archival item and 2020 readers’ poll are separate events. No full original recording was watched and no complete transcript comparison with Hansard was performed; the public text paraphrases the occasion without reproducing the speech or adopting every allegation it contains.

Read GPE’s own appointment release distributed by PR Newswire on 10 February 2014. It identifies Gillard as board chair, distinguishes the chief executive Alice Albright and the interim predecessor, and explains advocacy and fundraising plans. The 11 February Australian reports are later local publication dates. The 57-million out-of-school-children figure is a contemporary target population, not Gillard’s achieved enrolment count or personal donation. This is an institutional release, not independent evaluation of impact.

Read the Brookings biography paragraphs expressly giving GPE chairmanship 2014–2021 and Beyond Blue chairmanship 2017–2023. These dated descriptions take precedence over undated old present-tense biographies elsewhere. Its list of former roles and books is not an assertion that all posts remain current. The public profile does not invent exact GPE departure day, current Ducere chancellorship or complete publication review.

Read King’s College London’s 4 April 2018 institute announcement, identifying Gillard as founding chair and describing research, practice and advocacy. The release still speaks prospectively about that day’s launch event; use the establishment month without claiming to have witnessed the ceremony. A later King’s page reports an actual 11 April panel with Gillard, corroborating that activities followed. Current institute roles are corroborated separately in the October 2026 Hakluyt release. Old gender-representation figures and forecasts are not reused as 2026 statistics.

Read Wellcome’s 13 May 2020 appointment release. It announced succession to Eliza Manningham-Buller in April 2021; May 2020 was not the start of the chairmanship. The subsequent annual report establishes 12 April 2021 precisely. Chair of the Board of Governors is not chief executive or director responsible for all daily operations. Former GPE and Beyond Blue roles described in this 2020 announcement were contemporary at publication, not necessarily current.

Read Wellcome’s current chair profile. Its description of Gillard as chair is corroborated by the University of Melbourne’s October 2026 event report. However, its paragraph still calls her chair of Beyond Blue; that outside role is stale and is corrected using the December 2023 handover statements. Generic praise of transformed health/education systems is not an independent assessment. Published books and honours are not converted into unverified current appointments.

Read Gillard’s complete short statement dated 13 December 2023: stepping down as Beyond Blue chair at year-end, Sam Mostyn taking over from 2024, and Gillard remaining a patron. This corrects any assumption that she left in mid-2023 or remains board chair. The inclusive phrase seven years does not require exactly seven complete years elapsed; use the supported 2017–2023 range. Patron is not the same governance function as chair or chief executive.

Read Beyond Blue’s handover announcement, which says her term ends that month and she continues as patron. Cross-read with Gillard’s dated December statement to resolve the year-end succession. It confirms Sam Mostyn as incoming chair at that time, not necessarily current chair in November 2026. Claims about organisational service expansion and wellbeing benefits are institution-reported, not an independent programme evaluation.

Read Hakluyt’s 19 October 2026 appointment announcement syndicated through PR Newswire in AAP’s media-release section. It confirms membership of the international advisory board, chaired by William Hague, and describes her as current Wellcome chair, GIWL founding chair and Beyond Blue patron. It is company-supplied material, not independent AAP reporting. Its compressed biography incorrectly calls Brumby premier during her chief-of-staff employment; the Archives’ dated opposition-leader record is used instead. Advisory membership is neither corporate chairmanship nor an Australian government office.

Read the University of Melbourne’s 20 October 2026 report of the completed Climate CATCH Lab annual oration and preceding roundtable. The text identifies Gillard as Wellcome chair and describes actual participation and remarks, furnishing recent life-status evidence. Twenty October is publication, not an independently established event date. Calls for cooperation and institutional praise are not audited health outcomes. No photo pixels or recording were viewed, and the lab’s WHO collaborating-centre designation is not a personal appointment for Gillard.

Read the relevant governors-remuneration table in Wellcome’s 2022 annual report, page 82. It explicitly identifies Gillard as chair from 12 April 2021 and Manningham-Buller until 11 April 2021, sharpening the planned month in the May 2020 announcement. This is an actual historical role record, not an inference from the report publication date or the first day of April. No full financial-statement audit is claimed and remuneration figures are not republished.

Read selected current-role descriptions for Wellcome, GIWL and other activities. Its prospective June 2026 literary-prize phrasing shows not every section is current; no future event attendance or completed judging outcome inferred.

Read indexed 9 November 2026 excerpt on climate-related health preparedness. Opening returned a subscription page. No full interview, linked scientific study or future summit participation was reviewed.
Indexed official biography retrospectively confirms April 2021 Wellcome appointment; the annual-report table independently supplies the exact 12 April date. Full biography not separately opened.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No birth certificate, degree certificate, original migration dossier, complete policy-impact audit, full financial-statement review, speech/event recordings or portrait pixels were inspected. Distinguish institutional publicity from independent reporting, announced from actual dates, current from former outside offices, and board/advisory/patron roles. Refresh offices before publication and complete portrait visual inspection.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, history, licence review and EXIF; independently read the linked Flickr caption, upload/capture dates and its licence link to the CC BY-SA 2.0 deed. The photographer is Roberto Stuckert Filho/PR, while Dilma Rousseff names the publishing account. Original scene is a Cannes meeting on 2 November 2011; Flickr upload was 3 November. Commons reviewer Leoboudv confirmed the licence on 21 July 2013. Current 1227×1747 crop (491 KB) was uploaded at 00:26 on 24 August 2013 after a lower-resolution crop at 00:19; these are not new capture dates. Preserve photographer, account/source, title and crop notices plus share-alike terms. The old 334082-byte cache is absent. One original download on 18 November returned curl exit 22, 403 and reported HTTP 000. Identity, original colour, framing and sharpness remain unreviewed.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve 1961 Welsh birth and 1966 migration; law 1986 versus arts 1989; separate 2010 deputy and ministry end dates; 26 June 2013 party defeat versus 27 June effective resignation; minority government versus direct popular premiership; legislation versus implementation and long-term results; October 2012 speech versus later archive/poll; former GPE/Beyond Blue chair versus patron; Wellcome May 2020 announcement versus 12 April 2021 appointment; GIWL establishment versus later event; October 2026 report date versus precise lecture date; Hakluyt advisory member versus company chair or government official.
